content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a rubber band ball, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sort rubber bands by elasticity (10 minutes)
Step 2. Layer medium-sized bands over the core (15 minutes)
Step 3. Check the ball for any loose ends (2 minutes)
Step 4. Select the most durable bands for the foundation (5 minutes)
Step 5. Stretch extra-thick bands to reinforce the shape (8 minutes)
Step 6. Apply a cross-hatch pattern to the surface (12 minutes)
Step 7. Group bands by color for a decorative finish (15 minutes)
Step 8. Inspect the ball for spherical symmetry (3 minutes)
Step 9. Tighten the second layer of bands (10 minutes)
Step 10. Purchase bulk packs of rubber bands (1 hour)
Step 11. Clear a large workspace (10 minutes)
Step 12. Create a small paper wad for the center (2 minutes)
Step 13. Wash bands to remove factory powder (20 minutes)
Step 14. Dry the washed bands thoroughly (30 minutes)
Step 15. Wrap the paper wad with the first three bands (4 minutes)
Step 16. Research rubber band ball techniques online (45 minutes)
Step 17. Organize bands by width (10 minutes)
Step 18. Set aside broken bands for disposal (1 minute)
Step 19. Label the storage container (2 minutes)
Step 20. Measure the current diameter of the ball (2 minutes)
Step 21. Dust off the workspace (5 minutes)
Step 22. Wrap bands vertically around the ball (6 minutes)
Step 23. Inventory the remaining supply (15 minutes)
Step 24. Test the tension of the next batch (5 minutes)
Step 25. Add a layer of high-contrast colors (12 minutes)
Step 26. Pre-stretch the bands to prevent snapping (10 minutes)
Step 27. Count the total number of bands available (20 minutes)
Step 28. Prepare a non-slip mat (3 minutes)
Step 29. Clean the bands with a damp cloth (15 minutes)
Step 30. Sort bands by thickness (10 minutes)
Step 31. Twist the bands into figure-eights for double strength (7 minutes)
Step 32. Select bands with the best grip (4 minutes)
Step 33. Apply specialized UV-resistant bands (9 minutes)
Step 34. Buy a storage bin for the finished project (25 minutes)
Step 35. Read safety warnings about eye protection (5 minutes)
Step 36. Find a comfortable chair for the long task (5 minutes)
Step 37. Rotate the ball 90 degrees (1 minute)
Step 38. Set a timer for a work interval (30 seconds)
Step 39. Categorize bands by brand (20 minutes)
Step 40. Put on protective safety glasses (1 minute)
Step 41. Warm up hands and fingers (3 minutes)
Step 42. Weigh the ball on a digital scale (2 minutes)
Step 43. Consult a tutorial on maintaining roundness (15 minutes)
Step 44. Gather all stray bands from around the house (30 minutes)
Step 45. Find the original core materials (5 minutes)
Step 46. Photograph the progress (2 minutes)
Step 47. Watch a video on the "cloverleaf" wrapping method (10 minutes)
Step 48. Open all rubber band packaging (5 minutes)
Step 49. Wipe down the outer surface of the ball (3 minutes)
Step 50. Condition the bands with a light silicone spray (15 minutes)
Step 51. Discard any bands with visible dry rot (5 minutes)
Step 52. Bounce the ball to test its density (1 minute)
Step 53. Tighten any loose loops on the outer layer (4 minutes)
Step 54. Polish the outer surface (6 minutes)
Step 55. Arrange bands in a staging tray (10 minutes)
Step 56. Study the tension limits of the latex (15 minutes)
Step 57. Secure the final bands of the session (5 minutes)
Step 58. Take a short break to rest hands (10 minutes)
Step 59. Sort bands by length (12 minutes)
Step 60. Check for any protruding loops (3 minutes)
Step 61. Apply a layer of thin, tight bands (10 minutes)
Step 62. Test the bounce height (2 minutes)
Step 63. Calibrate the tension used for each wrap (8 minutes)
Step 64. Organize the workspace for the final phase (10 minutes)
Step 65. Set a goal for the final diameter (2 minutes)
Step 66. Sweep the floor of the work area (10 minutes)
Step 67. Document the number of bands used so far (5 minutes)
Step 68. Select the largest bands for the outer shell (5 minutes)
Step 69. Clean the storage bin (10 minutes)
Step 70. Place the ball in its display case (2 minutes)
